title: Stream-watermark-driven cutover controller for active-active edge failover
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Problem: Our hosted API edge must support active-active multi-region failover for long-lived streaming sessions (WebSocket/SSE/HTTP streaming). Current traffic-shift strategies are connection-centric and frequently break streaming continuity: clients either reconnect with new prefixes (losing prefix cache), or experience token duplication and partial responses. This increases error budget burn and causes SLA violations for low-latency streaming workloads.

Proposal: Implement a centralized 'cutover controller' that performs watermark-driven migration of streaming sessions during region shifts. The controller coordinates three coordinated mechanisms: 1) per-session stream watermarks persisted to the distributed KV cache (lightweight offset of last-acknowledged token), 2) a preflight resume handshake between source and target edge that ensures KV prefix availability, and 3) a tiered circuit-breaker + load-shedding policy anchored to SLO headroom during the shift.

Key features: 
- Watermark metadata: session_id -> last_emitted_token_index (TTL-managed). Stored in Redis/KV next to the prefix cache. Small writes per committed token (batched at 50–200ms) to limit write amplification.
- Preflight sync: target edge requests the session watermark and verifies prefix cache warmness. If prefix warmness < threshold, controller triggers one of: transient hedging to source, short-term redirect, or in-place rebuild strategy depending on SLO headroom.
- Stream resume handshake: client reconnect includes resume token and edge verifies watermark to avoid duplication/loss. Server-side dedupe uses token_index comparisons; fallback to protocol-specific trimming if mismatch.
- SLO-driven load shedding: controller evaluates request tier (free/dev/prod) and current error budget; if headroom is low, apply graded shedding: 1) delay (queue with bounded wait), 2) degraded response (non-streaming fallback), 3) reject with clear retry-after and fallbacks.
- Circuit tiers: soft circuit (per-route latency increase triggers), hard circuit (per-region overload), and session quarantine (short-term sticky routing to source region while background sync completes).

Trade-offs and constraints: 
- Consistency vs latency: Persisting watermarks increases write volume. We batch and async-ack to keep p50 unaffected but p99 may see slight increases under very high session churn.
- Storage TTL: Short TTLs mean lost watermarks on long idle sessions; we will surface an explicit resume-fallback UX to clients.
- Complexity: Introducing the cutover controller increases orchestration surface and adds an operation dependency (controller availability). We'll make it stateless with leader election and resilience patterns to reduce blast radius.

Rollout plan: 
1) Off-peak canary: deploy to staging and one low-traffic region behind a feature flag. 2) Synthetic streaming chaos tests (Simulate region drain + network partitions) and measure resume_success_rate and median-failover-latency. 3) Gradual ramp to 25% of cross-region shifts for production, evaluate metrics for 48h, then 100%. 4) Enable automated fallback policies based on observed headroom.

Metrics and success criteria: 
- resume_success_rate >= 99.5% for sessions < 30s interruption
- median failover latency <= 180ms for session handoff; p95 <= 800ms
- No increase > 5% in overall write QPS to KV during steady-state
- Error budget burn rate during shift < 1%

Observability and telemetry: 
- New tracing span: cutover.controller.prepare_sync, cutover.controller.handoff, cutover.controller.quarantine.
- Per-session telemetry: watermark_age_ms, prefix_warmness_score, handoff_path (direct/hedged/rebuild).
- Dashboards: shift success heatmap, shed/reject counts, per-region SLO headroom.

Testing and QA: 
- Unit tests for watermark durability, dedupe logic, and handshake timeouts.
- Integration tests with gateway and prefix cache emulator.
- Chaos experiments: region blackhole, KV write latency injection, and circuit firing under heavy load.

Docs and links: 
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/EDGE/Stream+Watermark+Cutover+Design
- Spike notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-example-spike
- Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge/pull/4123
- E2E tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-tests/actions/workflows/stream-cutover.yml

Follow-ups: 
- Evaluate adaptive watermark batching (50ms -> 200ms) to tune write amplification.
- Explore optional local persistent prefix cache (disk-backed) to reduce warmness dependency.
- Formalize client SDK resume semantics and error codes.
